Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Name: Preacher
Cardtype: Action
Discipline: Dominate & Presence
+1 stealth action. Requires an anarch.
[dom]  Make a ready younger non-anarch non-titled vampire anarch (and Independent).
[DOM] Unique. Put this card on this anarch and untap him or her at the end of the turn. As a +1 stealth  action, this anarch may use the [dom] ability above.

Can turn your vampires or the other's Methuselah anarch. Opens new options for decks expecting the other methuselah to have Anarch (Public ennemy, Camarilla segregation...)

Balanced? If not why?
Interesting? If not why?

Prince of Paris, France

Ratings Coordinator, Rules Director

Messages.Author: Mael
Messages.Body:
I don't like the ability to be able to make other peoples vampires anarch without them being able to get rid of it later.
I'd suggest at basic putting it on an opponents vampire with an option for them to burn it as an action, at superior putting it on your own vampire to allow him to make your own vampires anarch.
Also, for balance it should probably have either a cost, zero default stealth, or both. Both is probably too much, but I'd suggest testing with cost 1 blood as a +1 stealth action, or with cost zero as a zero stealth action.

For disciplines, pre/pot maybe? I think it's more in character for Brujah/!Brujah than for Ventrue. Disciplines would be too strong.

Edit: or how about
Name: Preacher
Cardtype: Action
Requires an anarch.
+1 stealth action. A ready younger non-anarch non-titled vampire you control becomes anarch and independent.
Put this card on a ready younger non-anarch non-titled vampire controlled by another methuselah, you still control this card. The vampire with this card is anarch. The vampire with this card may burn it as a D action that costs 1 blood.
+1 stealth action. Unique. Put this card on this anarch and untap him or her at the end of the turn. Once per turn this anarch may use the  ability above.

Edit again: the   should use a counter instead of putting the card on the vampire to not obstruct the uniqueness of the   ability.
Choose a ready younger non-anarch non-titled vampire controlled by another methuselah, and put a Preacher counter on them. A vampire with a Preacher counter is anarch. A vampire may burn their own preacher counter as a D action that costs 1 blood.

I'm not sure the phrase 'Preacher counter' doesn't really flow well, but you know what I mean? Also, I'm not sure who controls a 'counter' by default.

Messages.Author: Haze
Messages.Body:
I've found Anarch Revolts to be pretty good at encouraging vampires to go anarch, without necessarily forcing them to do so. It's a very interesting card!

This Preacher card idea just seems kind of annoying for the target, while being an inefficient use of actions for whoever's playing it. Instead of giving methuselahs an interesting choice, it brute-forces the issue in a dull way. And it's weak. Yech.

Messages.Author: Mael
Messages.Body:
> Haze wrote:
> There are better and faster ways of going anarch. it's weaker than "Go Anarch", and nobody uses that one.
>
I disagree, at  it's about on a par, different (as Blooding and Mustajib are different from each other), and lacking the untap. At superior it's more akin to a minion based version of Seattle Committee or Twilight Camp. Also, I have seen "Go Anarch" played, as has the TWDA.
>
> > The ability to make other people anarch is secondary, and can be used to help prevent the wrong person getting ousted by your anarch revolts,
> >
> cornercase, since they can go anarch themselves. maybe you save them 1 pool, sometimes.
>
It's not cornercase as they are would both be elements of the same deck so are under your control when deckbuilding. People play with Boons for pretty much the same purpose.
>
> > or to mess up a Black Hand or Aye/Orun deck that insists on leaving its key vampires not-anarch. The latter is why it needs to have a burn clause.
> >
> then it's just annoying at most, and they'll take the action to go un-anarch if needed. though actually, Black Hand vampires don't care if they're anarch, and it's hard to target a younger vampire with Orun...
>
No, but vampires who want to become black hand do, as do BH vampires who want to be Abbot. Also, it's quite easy to target a younger vampire with 1 or 2 Orun, and if the card prevented him ever becoming Laibon again that's all he'd ever get. And those are just the first two sect based strategies I thought of, probably not the only ones.

I'm not saying that you would include the card for it's ability to mess with such decks, but it's an added bonus on a card that you include in a deck to make your own guys anarch.
>
> why not just bleed for 1 instead of using this card
>
Why not just play Malk stealth bleed? Some people like a little variety. Apart from that, I really can't see how a card to make your guys anarch is comparable to bleeding for 1 as an action.

> Ankha wrote:
> Maybe the card was nerfed to much to become very useful.
> First version was the following, but I found it too powerful.
>
> Name: Preacher
> Cardtype: Action
> +1 stealth action. Requires an anarch.
> Put this card on this anarch and untap him or her at the end of the turn. During your untap phase, you may burn 1 blood to choose a ready younger non-anarch non-titled vampire. He or she becomes anarch (and Independent).
>
Agree that that's too powerful.
If you changed it to ...choose a ready younger non-anarch non-titled vampire you control. and added uniqueness to it, it would probably be balanced compared to Seattle Committee. When you include being able to change other players vampires sects then balance gets complicated.
